commitments: Every decodable voice parameter (reflection over the P01 Voice/Operator dataclasses) has at least one directed or boundary case; codec bookkeeping fields (operators container, channel_byte, anomalies, raw_bytes) are excluded and owned by the P01 test suite.
All 32 algorithms (codec indices 0-31) have at least one case; algorithms 4 and 6 have feedback-specific cases at feedback 0, 3 (mid) and 7.
Expectations are property-level (machine predicates or explicitly manual); no numeric comparison vectors arrive before N08.
Properties verified mechanically against the pinned oracle in reference/evidence/registry-smoke.json; manual rows are never guessed.
Corpus-selector cases reuse committed canonical hashes; voice bytes are not redistributed and resolve from the pinned archive at challenge gates.

synthetic_base.note: Fixture-like Mark I patch: loud sustained six-operator stack, algorithm 0, feedback 3. Cases override named fields on top of this base; overrides use op.<field> (all six operators), opN.<field> (operator N), <common field>, or the display name.

holdout.reason: acceptance thresholds are not frozen (N08); the holdout subset stays empty until the seal, and challenge runs must not draw from cases marked holdout before then

LFO waveform 0 with full pitch modulation renders audibly (waveform shape itself is a listening property).
LFO waveform 1 with full pitch modulation renders audibly (waveform shape itself is a listening property).
LFO waveform 2 with full pitch modulation renders audibly (waveform shape itself is a listening property).
LFO waveform 3 with full pitch modulation renders audibly (waveform shape itself is a listening property).
LFO waveform 4 with full pitch modulation renders audibly (waveform shape itself is a listening property).
LFO waveform 5 with full pitch modulation renders audibly (waveform shape itself is a listening property).
LFO speed 0 renders differently from speed 99 (one-sided difference claim; LFO-active renders are instance-dependent, see docs/REGISTRY-POLICY.md).
Fast LFO with full pitch modulation renders audibly.
LFO key sync off renders audibly; sync-phase behavior is instance-dependent and is a listening property (see docs/REGISTRY-POLICY.md).
LFO key sync on (restart at keydown) renders audibly.
Maximum LFO delay must produce an audible delayed ramp-in of the modulation (human judgment). Render must stay audible.
Zero pitch-mod depth leaves the note audible (unmodulated).
Full pitch-mod depth changes the render versus zero depth.
Pitch-mod sensitivity 0 renders audibly (unmodulated).
Pitch-mod sensitivity 7 changes the render versus sensitivity 0.
Zero amp-mod depth with AMS 3 renders audibly.
Amp-mod depth 99 with carrier AMS 3 changes the render (tremolo present).
Carrier amp-mod sensitivity 0 suppresses the tremolo the depth alone would give.

OBSERVED on the pinned oracle: oscillator key sync off and on render identically for repeated same-pitch notes (per-note phase is re-initialized at keydown regardless of data[136]). Recorded as observed reference behavior; the case stays directed for the frozen model (DEC-020 sync semantics).
Oscillator key sync on renders audibly (two-note phrase).
Slow segment-3 rate toward a low sustain level: the held note fades (rate=1 slowness is audible as a decay time).
Fast segment-3 rate reaches the low sustain level quickly; renders differently from the slow variant.
Delayed attack: with rate 1 into level 0 and a moderate rise rate, the note is silent through the early window and audible later.
Rising envelope segment: the carrier level rises from a low first target toward full output (rms grows over the first half second).
Nonzero final level with a slow release: the note-off tail is still audible at the end of the render window.
Fast release to a zero final level: the tail is fully gone by the end of the render.
Left scaling curve 0 at 32 semitones below the break point renders audibly.
Left scaling curve 1 at 32 semitones below the break point renders audibly; adjacent curves differ (curves 0-3 mutually distinct).
Left scaling curve 2 at 32 semitones below the break point renders audibly; adjacent curves differ (curves 0-3 mutually distinct).
Left scaling curve 3 at 32 semitones below the break point renders audibly; adjacent curves differ (curves 0-3 mutually distinct).
Zero left depth suppresses the curve-1 scaling the depth-99 variant applies.
Break point 1 puts note 40 right of the break, removing the left scaling.
Right scaling curve 0 above the break point renders audibly.
Right curve 3 at 36 semitones above the break point differs from curve 0.
Zero right depth suppresses the curve-3 scaling above the break point.
Rate scaling 0 at a low key renders audibly.
Rate scaling 3 speeds the same envelope at the low key versus scaling 0.
With carrier+modulator velocity sensitivity 0, velocities 30 and 127 render byte-identically (velocity must not leak into level).
Velocity 127 with sensitivity 0 renders audibly.
Velocity 30 with maximum velocity sensitivity renders audibly.
With velocity sensitivity 7, velocities 30 and 127 render differently.
Pitch EG starting above center and falling renders differently from the mirrored rising shape.
Pitch EG starting below center and rising differs from the flat pitch EG base.

OBSERVED on the pinned oracle: the patch transpose (data[144]) does not shift rendered pitch (the wrapper keydown omits the data[144]-24 shift that upstream Dexed applies). Recorded as a bounded R06 finding; the case stays directed for the frozen model (DEC-023 requires the patch transpose to be preserved).
Display name changes must not affect the render (name bytes are identity, not synthesis).
Same patch under a different display name renders audibly.
Repeated same-pitch note while held retriggers the envelope (render differs from the single-attack base).
Rekeying during release retriggers a fresh attack (differs from the held base).
Note-off without the pedal releases immediately (comparison anchor for the sustain-pedal case).
Sustain pedal holds the voice past note-off: later window is louder than the no-pedal variant; pedal-up at 1.0 s starts a release that decays.
Fifteen simultaneous notes sum audibly (voice-summation anchor).
Maximum voice summation: sixteen notes stay finite and bounded (peak <= 16 per-voice clip bound) while held.

OBSERVED on the pinned oracle: the 17th note is dropped (16-voice allocator finds no free voice and does not steal). Recorded as observed reference allocation behavior for N07; no inaudible substitution is possible because the render is byte-identical to the 16-note case.
All-sound-off (CC 120) kills the sounding voice: audible before, exactly silent after the event block.
All-notes-off (CC 123) releases (does not kill): the post-event window is quieter than the held base.
Full-up pitch bend changes the render versus centered bend.
Full-down pitch bend must be audibly lower (human judgment); mechanically it differs from both the centered and full-up renders.
Centered pitch bend renders audibly (no bend).

OBSERVED on the pinned oracle: mod-wheel CC 1 does not change the render because the pinned controller-modifier defaults leave the wheel inert (manifest mod_wheel_default_modifiers: range=0). Recorded as a bounded finding; the case stays directed for the frozen model (DEC-006 modwheel response).
Mod wheel at 0 renders audibly.
